key_insight: A synchronization-theoretic autoencoder reveals when cylinder–airfoil wake interactions suppress vortex shedding, enabling prediction of oscillation death from a learned low-order coordinate.
engineering_relevance: This provides a data-driven way to assess flow stability and interaction effects in body-body configurations, which is useful for designing quieter and more efficient fluid-based devices.
method: 2D incompressible DNS at Re = 100 for a cylinder with a downstream NACA0012 airfoil
Sweep geometry parameters: streamwise gap Δx, vertical offset Δy, and airfoil angle of attack α
Train a synchronization-theoretic autoencoder on aerodynamic coefficients to build a low-order coupled-oscillator model
evidence_signal: Parameter sweeps revealed four vortex-shedding regimes, including a suppressed-shedding state, and the learned coordinate supported theoretical prediction of flow stability.
watch_item: The approach is demonstrated for 2D, low-Reynolds-number flow, so broader applicability to higher-Re, 3D, or turbulent interactions still needs validation.
paper_title: Studying oscillation death in two-dimensional cylinder-airfoil interactions with synchronization-theoretic autoencoder
